deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Remark b) from p.36, in Grothendieck's preparatory notes for the IHES talk 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Nov-Dec 1967, published in Dix exposés). The topic is Monsky-Washnitzer (W-M) cohomology.

Setting: k is perfect of characteristic p, W = W(k), S = Spec W, K = Frac W, and X_0/k is smooth.

P.36 stated the W-M idea: the de Rham cohomology of a lift X of X_0 should, up to canonical isomorphism, not depend on the lift, and so be an intrinsic 'p-adic' cohomology of X_0. Remark b) observes that the published W-M papers suggest only H^i_DR(X/S) ⊗_W K (rational, not integral) has this invariance. They also treat only affine X_0.

This page adds the following.
- W-M work rationally ('et non p-adiques', i.e. not integrally p-adic). They lift X_0 neither as a scheme nor as a formal scheme, but as something resembling a Tate rigid-analytic variety: the weakly complete, or 'dagger', algebra A^†.
- For that reason they obtained only local invariants (affine pieces).
- By oral communication, W. (Washnitzer, presumably) says he has defined global invariants, over W and not only over K. He does this with the de Rham complex, working on the system of W-M lifts of the affine rings (reading uncertain). He also claims to have justified the assertions Grothendieck made.
- Remark c): by the comparison theorem, when X_0 lifts to X smooth over S, this construction yields H^i(X_0) with the right Betti numbers, namely those of the generic fibre X_t.

The next page explains why the naive formal-scheme approach fails. For the affine line, the de Rham cohomology of the p-adic completion W{t} is a 'monster': it is far too big. This motivates the dagger (overconvergent) completion.

Purpose: to situate crystalline cohomology against W-M cohomology. The issues in play are integral versus rational coefficients, globalization, and independence of the lift.
errors: Remark c) is stated with only the hypothesis 'X_0 lifts to X smooth over S'. That suffices for X proper. For affine or open X it is not enough: MW cohomology agrees with algebraic de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre only under extra hypotheses, e.g. a good compactification with relative normal-crossings boundary (Baldassarri-Chiarellotto and others).

The reported claim of global invariants 'sur W' (integral) is doubtful as stated. Integral dagger de Rham cohomology is badly behaved: even for the affine line, integrating t^i dt requires dividing by i+1, which produces unbounded p-torsion and non-finite-type groups. A good integral theory for non-proper varieties came only much later (crystalline cohomology for proper smooth X; later integral/overconvergent de Rham-Witt work). Grothendieck himself reports it only conditionally ('serait arrivé').

ideas.what: The W-M lift (weakly complete / dagger algebra) is viewed as an object resembling a Tate rigid-analytic variety, rather than a scheme or formal scheme.
ideas.modern_name: Dagger spaces / overconvergent rigid geometry; rigid cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (rigid cohomology, ~1981-86); Grosse-Klönne (dagger spaces, ~2000); Meredith, van der Put
ideas.where_published: Possibly only a brief mention of MW in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: MW cohomology is defined only for affine X_0 and is rational; the problem is to globalize it and to get integral (over W) invariants.
Comparison: for a smooth (proper) lift X, the p-adic cohomology of X_0 computes the de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre, hence gives the right Betti numbers.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorem between MW/rigid/crystalline cohomology and de Rham cohomology of a lift
ideas.where_published: Crystals paper (Dix exposés) discusses crystalline-de Rham comparison

missed.claim: A historical record that Washnitzer told Grothendieck, by 1967, that he had globalized MW cohomology and even defined integral (over W) invariants via the de Rham complex on the system of lifts. No such global integral theory by Washnitzer appears in the literature. Globalization is usually credited to van der Put and Berthelot in the 1980s.
missed.quote: Par communication orale de W., il serait arrivé à définir les invariants globaux (sur W, et non seulement sur K) en travaillant avec le complexe de De Rham sur la suite des relèvements
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historiographical detail about the prehistory of rigid cohomology. It suggests an unpublished, apparently abandoned attempt at global and integral MW theory.

missed.claim: In 1966-67 Grothendieck explicitly identifies MW weak completions as 'something resembling a Tate rigid-analytic variety'. This is the conceptual link later exploited by Berthelot's rigid cohomology and by dagger spaces.
missed.quote: mais en quelque chose qui ressemble à une variété rigide-analytique à la Tate
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early documented instance of the rigid-analytic viewpoint on MW cohomology, about 15 years before Berthelot. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: No new mathematics here. The page offers two historically interesting points: an early explicit remark that MW lifts are rigid-analytic in nature, and an otherwise unrecorded oral claim by Washnitzer about global and integral invariants. Both are minor historiographical details.
transcription_corrections: 'De ce fait, il vaut[?] définir[?] des [ ] par des invariants locaux' is more likely 'De ce fait, ils n'ont défini, dans [ ], que des invariants locaux' (they obtained only local invariants).
'sur la suite des relèvements de W_n[?] ... des anneaux W_n[?]' more likely reads 'sur la suite des relèvements de W.M des anneaux affines'.
'c) Ce serait[?], grâce au[?] K.[?] de comparaison[?]' is likely 'c) On voit(?), grâce au th. de comparaison'.
'(quand X_0 [-est-] relève en X lisse sur S)' should read '(quand X_0 se relève en X lisse sur S)'.
'— en tout cas[?] [-...-] de la fibre générique X_t' is probably '— ceux (struck) ... de la fibre générique X_t !'.
